Diagnosis.submission:
Root cause: Payment is rejecting a subset of Charge calls with an application-level 'Invalid token' rejection tagged with a gold loyalty-level attribute, and checkout surfaces that rejection to the frontend and load-generator as 'failed to charge card'. The rejection is raised inside payment's own request-handling code, arrives within 1-4ms (a fast business-logic decline, not a hang or timeout), and the payment span carries a flagd flag evaluation on the charge path. No deploy, image rollout or configuration edit exists for either payment or checkout in the 24-hour change log - the only entries are platform-automation first-creation records for the workload and service objects. A failure mode that (a) begins at a definite time (~15:11), (b) is segmented by a customer attribute rather than affecting all traffic, (c) is produced by the service's own code while the service stays up and keeps accepting traffic, and (d) leaves the change log empty, is a runtime flag flip in the flag store enabling a failing payment code path for gold-tier requests.
Faulty component: payment
Fault type: feature_flag
Confidence: medium

Evidence:
- In the failing checkout traces, the error consistently originates at the child span checkout/oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, which is marked ERROR with a payment rejection citing an invalid token and a gold loyalty-level attribute; the parent checkout/oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder then fails with a 'failed to charge card' wrapper. (found, from trace_query on checkout)
- The failing Charge child returns very fast, not slowly: the checkout-side Charge span is roughly 3.6-4.2ms in three traces and 40.6ms in one, and the downstream payment/oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge span returns in about 1.2-1.7ms (27.7ms in the one longer case). This is a fast-fail rejection, not a hang. (found, from trace_query on checkout)
- One trace at the start of the window (6dcefa8587bac50b) shows a different failure mode: the Charge child errors in 1.1ms with a transport dial/connection-refused error to a payment endpoint on port 8080, and no payment-service child span is produced at all, indicating the call never reached payment. (found, from trace_query on checkout)
- That same trace also carries an unrelated duration anomaly: a single currency/oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert child took about 1042ms, dominating the 1465ms root, while a later Convert in the same trace took about 2.3ms. No other sampled trace shows this. (found, from trace_query on checkout)
- In the remaining failing traces the checkout root spans are short (roughly 51-138ms) and the preparatory work (prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart) completes normally before the Charge call fails. (found, from trace_query on checkout)
- A downstream dependency of checkout other than payment (cart/valkey, product-catalog/postgresql, shipping, quote, currency) is causing the checkout failures. (ruled_out, from trace_query on checkout; why: All of those child spans complete successfully with sub-millisecond to low-single-digit-millisecond durations in every failing trace; none carry an error status.)

(ruled_out, from trace_query on checkout; why: Those spans are ERROR only as propagated parents; the deepest span bearing an originating error message is the checkout-to-payment Charge call, and the error text is reproduced upward unchanged.)
- The payment service is fully down or unreachable throughout the window. (ruled_out, from trace_query on checkout; why: Only the earliest sampled trace shows a connection-refused dial failure with no payment child span; the later traces show payment accepting the call, executing charge and a flagd flag evaluation, and returning a business-logic rejection.)

Reasoning:
Trace evidence [tr_0d3e77248cba] places the originating error at the deepest span - checkout's call to payment's Charge - with every other checkout dependency (cart/valkey, product-catalog/postgresql, shipping, quote, currency) returning clean and fast, and the frontend/load-generator spans erroring only as propagated parents. The same result rules out latency saturation: the erroring Charge spans return in ~1-4ms, far inside any deadline, so this is a decline rather than a wait. Payment's own logs [tr_5d6996bcab13] show the matching rejection, raised with a stack inside payment's code path, starting ~15:11:17 and recurring steadily to the end of the window, with nothing matching in the preceding ~28 minutes - so the condition has a sharp onset and is not background noise. The same result rules out a transport/infrastructure fault between payment and a dependency. [tr_407873775724] shows charge traffic still arriving at a steady cadence through the end of the window, which rules out payment being down, crash-looping, or cut off, and rules out a freeze or partition: payment is up, logging, and answering. Both change histories [tr_1778ce8ce3e6] and [tr_d3518340b0ba] contain only platform-automation creation records and explicitly no deployment, image rollout, config edit, or recorded flag toggle - which eliminates bad_deploy and an artifact/config-file change as the mechanism, and leaves a change that would not appear in a change log. The loyalty-tier attribute present on every rejection [tr_5d6996bcab13] plus the flag evaluation observed on payment's charge path [tr_0d3e77248cba] identify the mechanism as a flagged code path gated on a request attribute. Checkout itself is exonerated as the culprit: its logs [tr_60cfa54aac6a] contain no errors at all, only a bounded startup Kafka wait that resolved at ~15:10:33, well before onset. The sparse metric series on both services [tr_ab5bfd8c7f3b, tr_463410507be2] are too thin to corroborate or contradict anything and are cited only to record that they do not independently support a payment-internal volume-weighted regression.

Alternatives considered:
1. payment: A payment credential or token-validation setting holds a wrong value, so payment rejects charges it should accept. (bad_config). Ranked lower because: A statically wrong credential or validation setting would reject uniformly from process start, but the rejections begin at ~15:11 after the pod was already serving [tr_5d6996bcab13] and every observed failure carries the same loyalty-tier attribute, implying an attribute-gated branch rather than a globally wrong value. The change log [tr_1778ce8ce3e6] also records no config edit of any kind beyond the initial service-object creation.
2. payment: Payment's first-ever rollout at 15:09:59 brought up an artifact that cannot correctly service charge requests, and the failures are first-rollout breakage rather than a runtime toggle. (bad_deploy). Ranked lower because: The change log shows only workload creation with no image or version record to roll back to [tr_1778ce8ce3e6], and a broken artifact would fail every charge rather than a tier-segmented subset; the trace evidence also shows payment successfully executing the charge path and a flag evaluation before declining [tr_0d3e77248cba], which is working code taking a bad branch, not a broken build.

Open questions:
- The flag store itself was never queried. No specialist read flagd's configuration or history, so the specific flag name, its value, who or what set it, and the exact flip time remain unconfirmed - the flag evaluation span and the attribute-segmented rejection are circumstantial, not direct.
- Whether the rejection genuinely affects only gold-tier requests, or whether the loyalty attribute simply happens to be present on all sampled failures. Payment's charge-path logs [tr_407873775724] carry no branch-decision or reason line, so the segmentation cannot be confirmed from payment's own logging.
- The earliest sampled trace [tr_0d3e77248cba] shows a connection-refused dial to payment on port 8080 with no payment child span at ~15:10:56. This is unexplained and may be unrelated cold-start churn (payment's workload was created at 15:09:59) or may indicate a second, earlier fault.
- The ~1042ms currency Convert outlier in that same trace is unexplained and was not investigated; no currency specialist was dispatched.
- The error-ratio metrics for both services have empty baseline windows and traffic gaps [tr_ab5bfd8c7f3b, tr_463410507be2], so neither blast-radius magnitude nor onset shape (step vs ramp) is established. The claim that 13 services are affected rests on triage, not on measured evidence here.
- Nothing was gathered on the other nine alerted/affected services, so whether their symptoms all reduce to the checkout-to-payment path is inferred from trace topology rather than verified.
